summary: Team Nereon developed FireMaps, a web app that turns open NASA FIRMS satellite data into an interactive calendar of wildfire and agricultural burning activity. The MODIS and VIIRS sensors observe fires differently, which makes their records difficult to compare. FireMaps corrects for differences in satellite viewing angles and removes duplicate hotspot detections to build a consistent record. Users can select a region, explore daily activity, locate hotspots on a 3D globe and compare the same month across years. By showing when burning typically peaks and when activity departs from historical patterns, FireMaps helps fire managers and civil protection teams decide where to focus monitoring and when to prepare crews and resources.
details: FireMaps is a web application developed by Team Nereon that turns NASA FIRMS satellite detections into an interactive calendar of wildfire and agricultural burning activity. It combines historical and near-real-time records from MODIS and VIIRS, corrects for differences in satellite viewing angles, and removes duplicate detections so users can compare activity across sensors and years. Users can select a region, explore daily records in a colour-coded calendar, and locate hotspots on a 3D globe. One distinctive feature is the side-by-side view of raw and harmonised records, which shows how the corrections affect the results. Weather data from Meteomatics and environmental layers from JAXA and Copernicus help users interpret unusual activity. We built the prototype with C#, .NET, JavaScript, CSS, Python and Docker, and deployed it on Render. We considered differences in sensor resolution, reporting delays, API limits and the cost of weather data. Our goal is to help fire managers, civil protection teams and researchers spot changes in burning patterns, prioritise monitoring and plan staffing and resources ahead of peak periods.
